Motorcycle Touring Insurance Explained

Insurance isn't the most exciting part of tour planning, but it's among the most important. A proper touring insurance setup protects you, your bike, and your trip. Here's what UK motorcycle tourers need to understand.

Your Standard Motorcycle Insurance

Your regular motorcycle insurance policy covers riding on UK roads, but check these touring-specific details:

  • Mileage limits: Some policies have annual mileage limits. A 1,000-mile tour could push you over if you're on a low-mileage policy. Notify your insurer if needed.
  • Modifications: If you've added touring accessories (panniers, crash bars, heated grips), declare them. Undeclared modifications can void your policy.
  • Pillion cover: If you're riding two-up, ensure your policy covers pillion passengers.
  • Luggage and personal belongings: Most standard policies don't cover luggage or contents. You'll need separate cover for expensive gear.

Breakdown Cover

Breakdown cover is effectively insurance against mechanical failure, and it's essential for touring:

  • RAC and AA: Both offer motorcycle-specific policies. Ensure your policy includes recovery (not just roadside assistance) and covers you anywhere in the UK, including remote areas.
  • Home-start cover: Worth having — if your bike won't start on departure morning, you want someone who'll come to you.
  • Onward travel: Premium policies include onward travel — a taxi, hire car, or hotel if your bike can't be repaired same-day. Vital on multi-day tours.

Personal Accident Insurance

Your motorcycle insurance covers third-party liability, but what about you? Consider:

  • Personal accident cover: Pays out a lump sum for serious injury. Available as an add-on to many motorcycle policies or as standalone cover.
  • Income protection: If you're self-employed, an accident on tour could mean lost income. Specialist motorcycle income protection policies exist.
  • Medical travel insurance: If touring includes Channel Islands or Isle of Man, check whether your travel insurance provides cover. The NHS may not cover you in Crown Dependencies the same way.
The golden rule: read your policy documents before you tour, not after an incident. Knowing exactly what you're covered for — and what you're not — takes ten minutes and could save thousands.

Gear and Luggage Insurance

Your riding gear, camera equipment, and luggage can easily total £2,000-5,000. Standard motorcycle policies typically don't cover these.

  • Home contents insurance: Some policies cover personal belongings away from home. Check your existing policy.
  • Specialist gear insurance: Companies like Bikesure and Bennetts offer add-on gear coverage.
  • Gadget insurance: For cameras, phones, and action cams, specialist gadget policies may be cheaper than adding to your bike policy.

Insurance for Scottish Wild Camping and Offroad

If you venture onto unpaved roads, green lanes, or forest tracks during your tour, be aware:

  • Standard road insurance may not cover you on unpaved surfaces.
  • If you're riding maintained forest roads at sensible speeds, most insurers won't quibble. Dedicated off-road riding is a different matter.
  • Wild camping itself doesn't affect your insurance, but where you park your bike overnight might. Secure it properly.

Channel Islands and Isle of Man

Most UK motorcycle insurance policies automatically cover the Channel Islands and Isle of Man as they're Crown Dependencies. However, always confirm with your insurer before travelling. The same applies to Northern Ireland if your policy was set up for Great Britain only.

Pre-Tour Insurance Checklist

  • Confirm mileage is within your policy limits
  • Declare all modifications and accessories
  • Check breakdown cover includes recovery and onward travel
  • Review personal belongings and gear coverage
  • Ensure pillion cover if applicable
  • Download digital copies of all insurance documents
  • Save insurer's emergency phone numbers in your phone

Insurance is the safety net that lets you ride with confidence. Get it right before you leave, then forget about it and enjoy the road.
keyTakeaways: Check your policy's mileage limits before a long tour and declare all touring modifications and accessories.
Standard bike insurance rarely covers luggage or gear worth £2,000-5,000, so arrange separate cover.
Choose breakdown cover that includes recovery and onward travel, not just roadside assistance.
Most UK policies cover the Channel Islands and Isle of Man as Crown Dependencies, but always confirm.
Read your policy documents before you tour, not after an incident.

faq.q: Does my standard bike insurance cover touring?
faq.a: It covers UK riding, but check the details. Some policies have annual mileage limits that a 1,000-mile tour could exceed, so notify your insurer if needed. Declare all touring accessories such as panniers, crash bars and heated grips, because undeclared modifications can void your policy, and confirm pillion cover if riding two-up.

faq.q: Is my luggage and gear covered?
faq.a: Usually not. Standard motorcycle policies typically do not cover luggage or contents, yet riding gear, camera equipment and luggage can easily total £2,000 to £5,000. Check whether your home contents insurance covers belongings away from home, or arrange specialist gear cover from companies such as Bikesure or Bennetts, or a gadget policy for electronics.

faq.q: What breakdown cover do I need for touring?
faq.a: Choose a policy that includes recovery, not just roadside assistance, and covers you anywhere in the UK including remote areas. Home-start cover handles departure-morning disasters, and premium onward-travel cover provides a taxi, hire car or hotel if your bike cannot be repaired same day, which is vital on multi-day tours.

faq.q: Am I covered in the Channel Islands and Isle of Man?
faq.a: Most UK motorcycle insurance policies automatically cover the Channel Islands and Isle of Man because they are Crown Dependencies, but always confirm with your insurer before travelling. The same applies to Northern Ireland if your policy was set up for Great Britain only. Also note the NHS may not cover you the same way in Crown Dependencies.

faq.q: What is the golden rule of touring insurance?
faq.a: Read your policy documents before you tour, not after an incident. Knowing exactly what you are covered for, and what you are not, takes about ten minutes and could save thousands. Before leaving, confirm mileage, declare modifications, check breakdown recovery and onward travel, and save your insurer's emergency numbers in your phone.
